label.explanation: auth-svc briefly lost one of four instances (lines 152, 154) and was back within a minute (line 166). But account-svc retries 503s immediately with backoff disabled (lines 159, 167, 178, 187), multiplying load on auth-svc past its capacity so it keeps shedding (lines 175, 186, 198). The overload sustains itself long after the trigger; the shed requests (lines 174, 191, 200, 207, 218, 224, 242, 249) and edge 503s (lines 162, 173, 189, 197, 202, 212, 213, 220, 225, 240, 243, 247) are symptoms. Fix the retry policy / add a retry budget. The trigger was the auth-svc rollout, so bad_deploy is defensible, but a 1-of-4 rolling restart is routine — the retry amplification is the failure. Red herrings: line 68 (a routine disk usage warning on the log volume, nowhere near full); line 148 (a one-off slow reporting query on audit_log, not on the failing request path); lines 133, 142 (a deploy of audit-consumer, which is not on the failing request path and kept processing normally); line 144 (a single long GC pause in a healthy service, with heap well below limits).
